title: A Show for Two

storyBibleReview.storySpine: Kit wants a puppet show but dislikes his dog drawing; Zoe has a lively dog drawing but a collapsing paper stage, so Kit uses his building skill and Zoe uses her drawing to make one working show.

storyBibleReview.resolution: Kit supports Zoe’s scenery with his block stage, Zoe offers her paper dog, and both bring the puppet to life.
storyBibleReview.identityScope: Personal interests and complementary growing skills, without presenting them as fixed abilities or gender traits.

title: A Way Up

storyBibleReview.topicQuestion: How can a wheeled cart reach a model library above a step?
storyBibleReview.progression: Test a blocked vertical step, a steep short ramp and a gentler longer ramp reaching the same height.
storyBibleReview.synthesis: A ramp provides a continuous rolling route, and a gentler slope reduces the required uphill push under comparable conditions.

scienceSources.title: UC San Diego: Simple Machines
scienceSources.evidence: An inclined plane trades a longer path for lower force to raise the same load.

scienceSources.title: Concord Consortium: Forces and Motion Teacher Guide
scienceSources.evidence: A gentler slope requires less force for comparable surface/load conditions; friction matters. The book uses two smooth boards and the same cart.

storyBibleReview.scopeNote: A small model demonstration, not a building design or claim that a toy slope meets accessibility rules.

title: The Stretchy Bridge

storyBibleReview.storySpine: Kit wants to park his toy truck across a cloth river, but Zoe’s magic bridge is too short; extending it blocks the garage and shrinking it too early strands the truck, so they sequence the crossing before moving the empty bridge.
storyBibleReview.failedAttempt: Zoe shortens the bridge while Kit’s truck is on it, withdrawing its far end from the bank.
storyBibleReview.resolution: She restores the bridge, waits until the truck is off, then shortens and moves it so Kit can park.
storyBibleReview.magicRule: The toy bridge stretches lengthwise when Zoe says long and shrinks when she says short; its near end remains where it was placed. Its width and strength do not change. The toy truck has no magic.

title: Follow the Park Map

storyBibleReview.topicQuestion: How can a small map help someone find a real place?
storyBibleReview.progression: Match picture symbols to landmarks, align the map, trace a route and verify its destination.
storyBibleReview.synthesis: The map’s small pictures and paths represent a connected route through the real park.

scienceSources.title: National Geographic Education: Community Map
scienceSources.evidence: Maps represent places, and familiar picture symbols help early learners connect mapped objects and real landmarks.

scienceSources.title: National Archives: Analyze a Map
scienceSources.evidence: Map readers inspect symbols, represented places and the map’s purpose.

storyBibleReview.scopeNote: An invented small park with consistent picture symbols; not directions to an actual location or a scaled survey.

setting: World Discovery small enclosed park in daylight. Fixed plan: entrance gate at south/bottom; a straight path reaches one bench at a central fork; right branch passes one tall tree and reaches a kidney-shaped pond at northeast/top-right; left branch ends at a flowerbed. No roads.
props: One square paper park map with pictorial gate, bench, tree, pond and flowerbed connected by the exact established paths
One real brown bench

One curved pond
coverBrief: Kit holds the simple park map near the real pond; its blue kidney-shaped pond symbol matches the water beyond. The map has purposeful picture symbols and paths, no words or pseudo-writing.

title: Where Does Daylight Go?

storyBibleReview.topicQuestion: Why does one place on Earth move from day to night?
storyBibleReview.progression: Begin with fading daylight, introduce a spinning Earth and use a fixed flashlight and marked ball to model changing illumination.
storyBibleReview.synthesis: Turning the globe changes which place faces the light; the light does not need to circle it to make day and night.

title: A Dam Is Not a Home

storyBibleReview.topicQuestion: Is a beaver’s dam the same thing as its home?
storyBibleReview.progression: Follow branch placement into a dam, its effect on the pond, then distinguish the lodge and its underwater entry/dry chamber.
storyBibleReview.synthesis: The dam holds back water; the separate lodge provides a protected living space in that pond.

title: From Pond to Sky

storyBibleReview.topicQuestion: How does a water-living young dragonfly become a flying adult?
storyBibleReview.progression: Connect an adult to its egg and aquatic nymph, follow feeding and molts, then climb, emergence and wing expansion before the next generation.
storyBibleReview.synthesis: The same kind of animal grows in water and later flies, then eggs begin the water stage again.

scienceSources.title: Natural History Museum: Dragonflies, the Ultimate Hunters
scienceSources.evidence: Dragonflies begin as eggs, live as aquatic nymphs, molt repeatedly and emerge directly as adults without a pupa.

scienceSources.title: National Park Service: Species Spotlight, Dragonflies
scienceSources.evidence: Mature nymphs climb out, split their skin and emerge; adult bodies/wings expand and harden over hours.

scienceSources.title: Australian Museum: Dragonfly Life Cycle
scienceSources.evidence: Adult dragonflies have two pairs of wings and three pairs of legs; aquatic larvae are predators.

scienceSources.title: National Park Service: Common Green Darner
scienceSources.evidence: Green darner females insert eggs into plant material in water; aquatic nymphs molt, emerge through split skin and expand their adult wings. Female adults can have green thoraxes and brownish abdomens.

storyBibleReview.scopeNote: Illustrated green darner-type pond dragonfly, with natural aquatic nymph and adult anatomy; no butterfly-like pupa or cocoon. Timing is deliberately non-numeric because species vary.

storyBibleReview.topicQuestion: Does flying make a bat a bird?

title: The Apple Core Comes Back

storyBibleReview.topicQuestion: Can an old apple core help a new plant grow?
storyBibleReview.progression: Move scraps into a managed compost pile, show dry leaves/air/moisture and time, then use finished compost in soil for a new plant.
storyBibleReview.synthesis: Old food scraps become compost that improves growing soil rather than returning as intact food or instant soil.

storyBibleReview.scopeNote: A maintained garden compost bin, not a sealed bottle or an instant transformation. Finished compost is mixed into soil, never used as a substitute for all soil.
